device.name: Cat Printer MXW01 Mini Thermal Printer
device.notes:
Newest (2024/2025) cat-shaped mini thermal printer, sold as MXW01. Successor hardware to the GB01/MX05 family documented in device-specs/devices/cat-printer.yaml — it reuses the same 0xAE30 BLE service and AE01/AE02/AE03 characteristics, but speaks a DIFFERENT command protocol: frames open with 0x22 0x21 instead of 0x51 0x78, the command ID set is new, bulk image data moves to its own characteristic (0xAE03), and the legacy bit-reversal, lattice markers, and energy/speed commands are gone. Do not send the legacy command set to this model; the two families share nothing but the UUIDs. Fully local BLE, no cloud account, no pairing. The FEE7-family services seen on other cheap thermal printers do not appear in any MXW01 source.
FRAME FORMAT (commands to the printer on 0xAE01, responses and notifications from the printer on 0xAE02):
  [0x22 0x21 cmd_id 0x00 payload_len_le16] [payload] [crc8] [0xFF]
CRC8 is poly 0x07, init 0x00, no reflection, computed over the payload only — the same CRC-8 as the legacy family, via a 256-entry lookup table. (jeremy46231's PROTOCOL.md mislabels it "CRC-8/DALLAS-MAXIM"; the parameters it lists are plain CRC-8. Dallas/Maxim CRC-8 is poly 0x31 reflected.) Responses use the same layout, but the byte at frame offset 3 is not always 0x00 (observed 0x03 in some A1 responses), and the trailing CRC/footer may be absent — parse by the declared length and treat CRC and 0xFF footer as optional (moblin's parser doesn't read them at all; jeremy46231's checks them only when present).
COMMANDS:
  0xA1 get_status — payload 0x00; reply payload layout below.
  0xA2 set_intensity — 1 byte 0x00-0xFF print darkness (0x5D is a
      sane default; >150 risks scorching paper).
  0xA3 eject_paper — uint16 LE line count.
  0xA4 retract_paper — uint16 LE line count.
  0xA7 query_count — unknown purpose; reply is often all 0xFF.
  0xA9 print_request — payload [uint16 LE line_count, 0x30, mode]:
      mode 0x00 = 1bpp mono, 0x02 = 4bpp grayscale; 0x01 observed
      as a mono variant that ejects less paper at the end. Reply
      payload[0] 0x00 = accepted.
  0xAA print_complete — unsolicited notification when the physical
      print run finishes.
  0xAB get_battery_level — payload 0x00; reply payload[0] = level.
  0xAC cancel_print — payload 0x00.
  0xAD print_data_flush — payload 0x00; sent after the last AE03
      data chunk to kick off printing.
  0xB0 get_print_type — payload 0x00; reply payload[0] is a type
      code (0x01, 0xFF, other seen; meaning unclear).
  0xB1 get_version — payload 0x00; reply payload holds a UTF-8
      version string plus a type byte (observed 0x31/0x32,
      interpreted in the vendor app as low/high-voltage printhead
      variants).
  0xB2, 0xB3 — unknown; vendor-app comments hint at "learn" and
      "sign/encryption" functionality (via MaikelChan).

STATUS RESPONSE (0xA1) payload layout (offsets relative to the payload, matching the MaikelChan and moblin parsers):
  payload[0] state: 0 standby, 1 printing, 2 feeding paper,
    3 ejecting paper
  payload[3] battery level (approximate)
  payload[4] head temperature (approximate)
  payload[6] overall flag: 0 = OK, non-zero = error
  payload[7] error bitmask when flag != 0: bit0 (0x01) no paper,
    bit2 (0x04) overheated, bit3 (0x08) low battery; 0x09 = no
    paper + low battery observed
Note: jeremy46231's PROTOCOL.md lists these same fields at "Payload[6..13]" because that document's payload indices include the 6-byte frame header — subtract 6.
IMAGE DATA: 384 pixels wide. 1bpp: 48 bytes per row, LSB = leftmost pixel, black = 1 (NOTE: unlike the legacy family there is NO bit reversal). 4bpp grayscale: two pixels per byte, high nibble first, 192 bytes per row, values 0-15. Stream rows top-to-bottom as raw bytes on 0xAE03 (write without response). The printer has no explicit flow control — pace writes: working implementations use 48-byte row chunks with ~15 ms gaps or MTU-sized chunks with ~100 ms gaps. Pad the buffer with 0x00 to at least 4320 bytes (90 rows); shorter buffers do not print.
PRINT SEQUENCE:
  1. Connect; discover service 0xAE30; subscribe to 0xAE02.
  2. (Optional) set_intensity (0xA2).
  3. get_status (0xA1); wait for the 0xA1 response; abort unless
     the overall flag is 0.
  4. print_request (0xA9) with line count and mode; wait for the
     0xA9 response; payload[0] must be 0x00.
  5. Stream the (padded) image buffer on 0xAE03, paced as above.
  6. print_data_flush (0xAD).
  7. Wait for the 0xAA print_complete notification; scale the
     timeout with line count (~15 lines/sec plus a base margin).
  8. (Optional) eject_paper (0xA3) to advance past the tear edge.

Paper emerges bottom-first relative to the image buffer; rotate the image 180 degrees client-side if it should exit right-side-up (jeremy46231's tool does this by default).
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for UUIDs, frame format, command IDs, the print sequence, and the 1bpp encoding — three independent hardware-tested implementations agree: MaikelChan/CatPrinterBLE (C#, tested on a purchased unit), jeremy46231/MXW01-catprinter (Python/bleak, ships PROTOCOL.md), and eerimoq/moblin (Swift MXW01 support in production). 4bpp grayscale and the A3/A4/B0/B1 commands are implemented and exercised by MaikelChan only (MEDIUM). The status payload offset note above, A7, B0, B2 and B3 remain LOW confidence. Not verified against hardware by this project — testing.status stays untested.

credentials.notes: BLE-only. No auth. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state. Power-cycling resets the connection.

steps.action: Turn printer off and on again.

methods.description: Scan for a BLE advertisement named MXW01 carrying service UUID 0xAE30 (or 0xAF30), connect, subscribe to 0xAE02, and follow the printing sequence.

steps.action: Power the printer and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and execute the documented printing sequence.

setup.notes: No provisioning. The printer advertises the 0xAE30 service under the name MXW01 as soon as it is powered on. No pairing or bonding is required by any known client. macOS quirk inherited from the legacy family: CoreBluetooth/Bleak can surface the service as 0xAF30 instead of 0xAE30 — tolerate both (moblin scans for 0xAF30 outright; jeremy46231 accepts either).

rejoin.notes: No persistent bonding. Any central within range can connect.

variants.notes: The only model known to speak this protocol. The vendor app's "HD" print option is believed to be the 4bpp grayscale mode.

features.notes: 48 bytes per row, LSB = leftmost pixel, no bit reversal (unlike the legacy family). 4bpp grayscale (192 bytes/row, high nibble first) via print mode 0x02.

characteristics.name: Control (Client → Printer)
characteristics.notes: Write channel for all framed commands (0xA1 status, 0xA2 intensity, 0xA3/0xA4 paper, 0xA9 print request, 0xAD flush, 0xAB battery, 0xB0/0xB1 info).

characteristics.name: Notify (Printer → Client)
characteristics.notes: Command responses (0xA1 status, 0xA9 print accept, 0xAB battery, 0xB0/0xB1 info) and the unsolicited 0xAA print_complete notification. Subscribe before sending commands. Responses may omit the CRC/footer — parse by declared length.

characteristics.name: Data (Client → Printer)
characteristics.notes: Bulk image data only — raw unframed rows, 48 bytes/row 1bpp or 192 bytes/row 4bpp. No flow control; pace chunk writes (~15 ms per 48-byte row, or ~100 ms per MTU chunk).

services.name: MXW01 Printer Service
services.notes: Single custom service carrying the whole protocol — same service UUID as the legacy cat-printer family, but the MXW01 frames open with 0x22 0x21 (not 0x51 0x78) and use a new command set. Command frame: [0x22 0x21 cmd_id 0x00 payload_len_le16] [payload] [crc8(payload)] [0xFF]; CRC-8 poly 0x07 init 0x00 over the payload only. May surface as 0xAF30 on Apple platforms.
